parish partnership name throughout the diocese parishes are being called to come together in new forms. grouping, cluster, amalgamation of parishes are the way ahead for the diocese that is reduced in priests to service local areas. we are privileged that the parish of saggart, rathcoole, brittas and the parish of newcastle have been working together for many years. a shared parish pastoral council and finance committee has been in place for a number of years showing a shared interest and cooperation between the ‘four districts’. we have been invited to discern a common name that has a resonance throughout the area. one suggestion raised recently was “mo sacra” a saint from the 7th century who set up a monastery in what is currently saggart cemetery. st brigid’s well in rathcoole, st. finian’s well in newcastle are other names. have you any thoughts or suggestions on a name that could be used. bethany bereavement support group is a voluntary community and parish-based service. our ob jective is to support the bereaved through the grieving process and our services are totally free of charge a nd confidential within the law. the name bethany is derived from the story of jesus’ friends martha & mary who lived in a village called bethany and grieved over the death of their brother lazarus. visit

sunday 7th and 8th november share appeal sunday takes place on the weekend of november 7th and 8th, highlighting the important work that is funded by the weekly collection. the share newsletter is available to read on the parish website and there is a copy on the noticeboard in the church foyer. we would like to thank all our parishioners for their continued support. gaisce & transition year: volunteer with the parish is there a young person in your family (a son, daughter or grandchild) in transition year or older and looking for a gaisce community involvement activity? st. fintan’s parish is running a parish participation programme for 2026/2027. students help organise and run parish events alongside our liturgical team and volunteers. roles include music, coordination, preparing materials and power point for mass, hospitality in the parish centre, and leading parts of events. opportunities run throughout the year, from the family masses and holy week to the life in the spirit course and the visit of the relics of st. carlo acutis in january. every event a student takes part in is signed off by the parish, and a confirmation form is provided for their school’s gaisce leader (pal) or ty coordinator. to find out more or to sign up, contact fr. paul hampson at
pa_hampson@yahoo.com
